questions.question: How many types of Bihu festival are celebrated in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bihu is a set of three important Assamese festivals in Assam – 'Rongali' or 'Bohag Bihu' observed in April, 'Kongali' or 'Kati Bihu' observed in October, and 'Bhogali' or 'Magh Bihu' observed in January.
 
• The Rongali Bihu is the most important of the three, celebrating the spring festival.
 
• The Bhogali Bihu or the Magh Bihu is a harvest festival, with community feasts.
 
• The Kongali Bihu or the Kati Bihu is the somber, thrifty one reflecting a season of short supplies and is an animistic festival.
 
• The Rongali Bihu coincides with the Assamese New year.
 
• Assamese celebrate the Rongali Bihu with feasts, music, and dancing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Bohag Bihu Or Rongali Bihu is one of the major festivals of Assam.
 
• Commonly known as Rongali Bihu, it is celebrated in Assam during the middle
 of the month of April.
 
• This festival celebrates the onset of the Assamese New Year (around April 15) and the coming of Spring.
 
• This marks the first day of the Hindu solar calendar and is also observed in Bengal, Manipur, Nepal, Orissa, Punjab, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu though called by different names like Pongal in south India, Baisakhi in north India.
 
• This festival is celebrated for the whole month.
 
• The new year of the Assamese calendar usually falls on April 15. The new year
 starts with the month of Bohag. This is the reason why Rongali Bihu is also called
 Bohag Bihu.
 
• The word Rongali is derived from Rong which means Happiness and celebrations. So this festival represents the happiness of society.
 
• On the eve of Rongali Bihu, the womenfolk clean their clothes and prepare special Bihu delicacies like Chira, Pitha, etc. In the rural areas, the menfolk remain busy collecting necessary items such as Tara Pogha (ropes for the cattle) prepared out of slices of Tara (an indigenous creeper) and vegetables such as raw turmeric, brinjal, gourd, etc for the next day's Garu Bihu.

questions.question: 'Ram Navami' is celebrated in India to commemorate the:

options.text: coronation ceremony of Lord Rama as a king.
return of Lord Rama from forest.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**birth of Lord Rama**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ram Navami** is a Hindu festival that celebrates the birth of Lord Rama, the seventh avatar of the god Vishnu.
 
• It falls on the ninth day of the Hindu lunar calendar month of Chaitra, which typically occurs in March or April.
 
• Lord Rama is believed to have been born at noon, and this time is marked by special prayers and rituals.
 
• The festival is celebrated with various activities including fasting, singing devotional songs, reading the Ramayana, and visiting temples.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Significance of Ram Navami**

 
 
• Ram Navami marks the descent of Vishnu as Lord Rama, who is considered a symbol of virtue and chivalry.
 
• Lord Rama's story is chronicled in the ancient Indian epic, the Ramayana, which is revered by Hindus worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Celebration Practices**
 
 
• Devotees clean and decorate their homes, perform puja (worship), and recite verses from the Ramayana.
 
• Many people observe a day-long fast, breaking it only after performing evening prayers.
 
 
 
• **Temples and Public Celebrations**
 
 
• In Ayodhya, the birthplace of Lord Rama, grand celebrations are held with processions, and the city is illuminated with lights.
 
• Temples dedicated to Lord Rama organize special events, including recitations of the Ramayana and theatrical performances of his life story.
 
 
 
• **Symbolic Importance**
 
 
• Lord Rama's life and deeds exemplify righteousness, moral values, and the importance of fulfilling one's duties.
 
• Ram Navami serves as a reminder of these virtues, inspiring devotees to embody these qualities in their lives.

__
 
• Known as the '100 Drum Festival', the Wangala Festival is a traditional festival in the northeastern Indian state of Meghalaya.
 
• The festival kicked off on November 12th, 2021.
 
• The festival lasts from two days to a week. 
 
• It is one of the most important festivals of the Garo Tribe.
 
• The tribesmen make sacrifices to please their god Saljong. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Wangala festival marks the end of a period of toil, that brings good results to the fields which also signifies the onset of winter.
 
• It is also celebrated in honour of the Sun God that marks the end of the long harvest season.
 
• Wangala is celebrated with different forms of dance.
 
• These dances are performed on the tunes of folk songs that are played on drums and primitive flute.
 
• Additionally, these flutes are made of buffalo horns.
 
• On the first day of the festival, people celebrate it with a ceremony called Ragula.
 
• This ceremony is performed in the house of the village’s chief.
 
• Then on the second day of celebration, which is called Kakkat, people begin the ceremony by dancing to the rhythms of long oval-shaped drums.
 
• In this celebration, young and old join together while men play the drums and women perform traditional dance forms. The dance form is known as Dama Dagota.

questions.question: Hanukkah is a ______ festival.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jewish**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hanukkah, also known as the **Festival of Lights**, is a Jewish holiday celebrated for eight days and nights.
 
• It commemorates the rededication of the Second Temple in Jerusalem during the second century BCE after its desecration by the Seleucids.
 
• The holiday is observed by lighting the menorah (a nine-branched candelabrum), with one additional candle lit each night.
 
• Traditional foods such as latkes (potato pancakes) and sufganiyot (jelly-filled doughnuts) are consumed, symbolizing the miracle of the oil that burned for eight days.
 
• Hanukkah typically falls in November or December, according to the Jewish lunar calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Menorah:** The menorah is a central symbol of Hanukkah, consisting of eight branches for the eight days of Hanukkah and one additional branch for the shamash (helper candle).
 
• **Miracle of the Oil:** According to Jewish tradition, a small amount of oil sufficient for one day miraculously burned for eight days during the rededication of the Second Temple.
 
• **Dreidel:** A traditional four-sided spinning top used during Hanukkah, with Hebrew letters symbolizing the phrase "A great miracle happened there."
 
• **Historical Context:** Hanukkah commemorates the victory of the Maccabees, a group of Jewish rebels, over the Seleucid Empire and the subsequent restoration of Jewish worship in the temple.
 
• **Significance:** Hanukkah is a celebration of religious freedom, resilience, and the perseverance of Jewish identity and traditions.

questions.question: Which festival from West Bengal has found a place in the UNESCO list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Durga Puja**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Durga Puja**, a major Hindu festival celebrated in West Bengal, was inscribed on the **UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** in December 2021.
 
• It is recognized for its **rich cultural traditions, artistic expressions, and community participation** that transcend religious boundaries.
 
• The festival involves intricate idol-making, vibrant processions, cultural performances, and traditional rituals, showcasing the **creative and spiritual heritage of Bengal**.
 
• Durga Puja is celebrated annually during the autumn season and honors the victory of Goddess Durga over the demon Mahishasura.
 
• The recognition by UNESCO highlights the festival's **global cultural significance** and its role in fostering social cohesion and cultural diversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage:**

 
 
• Established in 2003, this list aims to safeguard practices, representations, expressions, knowledge, and skills that communities recognize as part of their cultural heritage.
 
• India has several elements inscribed on this list, including Yoga, Kumbh Mela, and now Durga Puja.
 
 
 
• **Durga Puja Celebrations:**
 
 
• It spans over 10 days, with the last five days being the most significant, including **Shashthi, Saptami, Ashtami, Navami, and Dashami.**
 
• Dashami marks the immersion of the Durga idols, symbolizing the return of the goddess to her celestial abode.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• Durga Puja generates significant economic activity, especially in Kolkata, with expenditures on pandals, decorations, cultural programs, and food.
 
• It also serves as a source of livelihood for artisans, craftsmen, and workers involved in the festival.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO and India:**
 
 
• India has 14 intangible cultural heritage elements inscribed on the UNESCO list as of 2023.
 
• This recognition enhances global awareness of India's rich cultural traditions and promotes tourism.

__
 
• **Ugadi** is one of the famous festivals celebrated among **the Hindus** with great pomp and fanfare. **Ugadi** is celebrated as the New Year of the **Telugu** and **Kannada people**.

• According to the Hindu lunisolar calendar, Gudi Padwa is observed on the first day of Chaitra, which, according to the Gregorian calendar, often occurs between March and April.

• It is celebrated in the month of January every year.
 
• The harvest festival is named after the Tamil word, Ponga, which means to boil.

• The second day of Pongal is known as Surya Pongal and is dedicated to the Sun God.
